item: review item: correct the dudect inversion harness and measure the flagged implementation

candidate.note: the same DSO the ctgrind matrix and the branch audit used, so those instruments and this one are bound to one artefact; the OpenSSH matrix cell DSO ee7fa27c is a different link (build_trees.sh passes libcrypto.ld's version script, the timing link did not) and no claim is combined across the two

harness_change.before: one `inverse` mode, no BN_FLG_CONSTTIME set, operands of differing length; it measured the variable-time dispatch and its leak verdict was read against the constant-time kernel
harness_change.after: inverse_vt (unflagged, differing lengths), inverse_ct (flagged, equal lengths), inverse_ct_len (flagged, differing lengths), inverse_ec (flagged, modulo the P-256 order obtained from EC_GROUP_get_order); each prints the flag read back and counts operation success, and a failed operation rejects the measurement (exit 3)
harness_change.what_the_harness_can_establish: that the flag was stored and that the inversion succeeded; which implementation ran is witnessed by the ctgrind case bn::arith::tests::ctgrind_secret_mod_inverse (taint), not by this timing harness. The two instruments are presented together; neither alone is evidence of constant-time behaviour.

exit_code_semantics.3: this harness: a measured operation failed, so the timings are rejected

observations: the earlier inverse result (max |t| 485, leak) is reproduced as inverse_vt at 1002.46: it was the variable-time path, exactly as the review suspected
the flagged inversion shows no leakage evidence at these sample sizes: inverse_ct 1.38, inverse_ct_len 1.91, inverse_ec 2.17, all state 1 — the same order as modexp (2.09 / 1.05)
inverse_ct_len compares two operand lengths (200 vs 254 bits) and did not separate them at this sample size; the crate documents the normalised length as public metadata regardless
no mode exited 3 and every BN mode reports 0 failed inversions, so no measurement was taken on a failure path
limits: dudect state 1 is 'no leakage evidence yet', not a constant-time proof; absence of detected leakage is not proof of constant-time behaviour
sample size 20 000 per batch, three batches, one host, one build
the harness measures the inversion call; it does not measure the surrounding ECDSA arithmetic, whose ctgrind counts (813 061 errors over 128 contexts) remain the open finding
